title: This Stray Cat Turned Out to Be the First New Cat Species Discovered in Over a Century - Nautilus
gist: A stray kitten raised by a Bolivian man turned out to be Leopardus tilcayo, a newly described wild cat from the Bolivian Yungas cloud forest and the first new cat species found in over a century. Irregular spots and genetic tests against 37 other tropical cats confirmed it.

insights.claim: Leopardus tilcayo, described after a Bolivian man handed a stray 'kitten' to a wildlife refuge, is reported as the first new cat species discovered in over a century.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Shows how much biodiversity remains undescribed in Andean cloud forests; relevant to conservation and land-use debates.
insights.locator: Imagine scooping up a stray kitten

insights.claim: Leopardus tilcayo is smaller than a house cat, about 17 to 20 inches long plus a roughly 10-inch tail, and lives in the Bolivian Yungas cloud forest at the foot of the Andes.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Habitat-specific species discoveries can bring new protection pressure on the Yungas region.
